A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Training-Free Bayesianization (TFB) work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial experimental and organizational revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original TFB experiments on reasoning tasks, distribution shifts, different backbones, LoRA variants and last-layer Bayesianization in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional Llama3.1-8B comparisons, synthetic regression, computational costs and anchoring analyses in Section 5 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The SVD reparameterization, inverse-singular-value noise scaling, variance-maximization constraint, posterior averaging and last-layer option are retained. Binary search and parallel grid/interpolation search already appear in v1; v2 changes their experimental use without introducing a new core algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds a small synthetic cubic-regression task and evaluates anchoring on unlabeled test inputs, representing partial access to user inputs. The six commonsense datasets, combined task and chemistry/physics distribution-shift tests remain.

E2.justification: The new primary Llama3.1-8B comparison omits Bayes By Backprop (BBB), which participated in v1's primary comparison. BBB remains in the relocated Llama2-7B comparison, v2 Table 15. MCD, ENS, LAP, BLoB, MLE and MAP remain represented.

E3.justification: The primary comparison switches from Llama2-7B after 5,000 steps to Llama3.1-8B after five epochs. Anchor tuning changes from accuracy, adaptive 1%/0.5% tolerances and grid/interpolation search to 500 pseudo-labeled examples, NLL, 0.3% relative tolerance and five-step binary search over [0.001, 0.015]. The reported shared maximum learning rate changes from 1e-4 to 2e-4.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds regression uncertainty visualization, Bayesianization time/memory comparisons, anchor-size sensitivity, training-versus-test anchoring and NLL-versus-accuracy analyses. Family and last-layer analyses are revised for Llama3.1-8B. Conversely, v1 Tables 8–9's detailed tolerance sweeps and test-ECE-optimized comparisons are not retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark means and standard deviations over three seeds. v2 additionally reports searched noise scales averaged over three seeds in Table 7, whereas v1 specifies a single-seed grid search. Figure 2 introduces predictive standard-deviation bands from ten sampled weight configurations.

E6.justification: v2 reports extensive new Llama3.1-8B and diagnostic results under revised settings. v1 Table 1 is numerically unchanged in v2 Table 15; Tables 3–5 and the backbone/PEFT breakdowns also retain their values. Earlier tolerance/oracle result entries disappear. Some new reported findings conflict: Appendix F.6 quotes WG-S ECE of 8.78%, while its corresponding Table 11 reports 3.04%.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.2 relaxes the prior-scale condition from σp ≫ ε0 to σp > ε0 and explicitly quantifies positive λ. v2 identifies ordinary variational inference as the λ = 1/|D| case and adds an explicit projection proposition in Appendix D. The principal derivations remain largely unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace the general claim of equivalence to variational inference with equivalence to KL-regularized variational optimization/generalized variational inference. The central training-free Bayesianization, applicability and calibration contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of anchor robustness and dataset/batch-dependent computational tradeoffs, qualifies search optimality through monotonicity, and softens the expressiveness limitation while recommending TFB first. Some new interpretations overreach: Appendix F.4 calls anchor-source effects negligible, although Table 10 gives MLE+TFB chemistry ECE of 14.63% with training anchors versus 29.72% with test anchors.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies baseline details including MAP weight decay, dropout rate, ensemble size and Bayesian-Torch usage, plus regression implementation and single-A100 hardware information. It removes v1 Section 5.4's fixed backbone-specific noise scales despite retaining those results. Both versions still promise code at the same project location.

R1.justification: v2 adds generalized/weighted variational-inference positioning through Knoblauch, Higgins and Khan citations, alongside Adam, Bayesian-Torch and natural-parameter-network references supporting implementation and regression. The original Bayesian LoRA discussion is largely preserved in Appendix C.

P1.justification: Method explanations and experimental narratives are extensively revised. Notation moves into the method section; the algorithm, limitations and longer related-work discussion move into appendices. The appendix organization changes from A–C to A–F, including relocation of the earlier main experimental discussion.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensively reflowed tables and new color highlighting. v2 adds a framework diagram, regression panels and anchor-size plots as Figures 1–3, alongside new computational and comparison tables. Existing displays are also resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful computational measurements, anchoring controls, reproducibility details and more precise generalized-VI framing. However, it removes earlier tolerance/oracle analyses and introduces reporting conflicts: Appendix F.6 disagrees with Table 11, and Table 9 duplicates all four OOD ECE entries in an accuracy row. These problems obscure the reliability of important new analyses, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
